stories.headline: NFL flexes Browns-Raiders to replace Pats-Chargers in SNF slot for Week 12
stories.summary: The NFL has flexed the Browns-Raiders Week 12 game into NBC's "Sunday Night Football" slot.
stories.body:
The NFL has flexed the Cleveland Browns-Las Vegas Raiders Week 12 game into NBC's "Sunday Night Football" slot, the league announced Tuesday.

The Nov. 29 matchup will replace the previously scheduled New England Patriots-Los Angeles Chargers game, which will move to the 4:05 p.m. ET slot.

Instead, Cleveland will host Las Vegas in a primetime game that will have huge implications in the AFC playoff race.

The Browns (6-4) currently are the AFC's seventh seed, holding the third and final wild card spot in the conference. Cleveland is 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963.

The Raiders (4-6) are two games behind Cleveland in the standings. Las Vegas lost to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 10 in No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza's first career start. The Raiders will face the Denver Broncos on the road in Week 11.

stories.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
stories.summary: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
stories.body:
Hot stove season has finally begun!

The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter -- which is expected to include a labor stoppage -- unfolds.

Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here -- this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.

Related links: Tracker | Top 50 free agents

White Sox add midrotation piece with May
The deal: Three years, $52.5 million

Grade: D+

We've had two significant signings off the free agent market so far, and both involve freshly minted ex-Milwaukee Brewers: After Jake Bauers landed with the Boston Red Sox on Friday, the Chicago White Sox plucked Dustin May off the championship Milwaukee pitching staff.

Whereas Boston was banking on Bauers' 2026 breakout being his current true talent level, the White Sox are perhaps taking a bigger gamble that May's past five years do not represent his real level of ability. Since his early shine as a top Los Angeles Dodgers prospect, which included some promising early work in the majors, May's career has been journeyman-like. Around injuries that cost him the 2024 season, he has put up 0.9 bWAR with a 91 ERA+ over 356 big-league innings for the period covering 2022 through last season.

May became a fallback addition for the Brewers at the 2026 trade deadline after more glitzy pursuits (ahem, Tarik Skubal) fell short. May put up a 106 ERA+ for the St. Louis Cardinals before the trade and, given the Brewers' track record with acquired pitchers, you had to figure the move boded well for an even better post-trade performance. But that's not what happened. May had a 5.65 ERA and 75 ERA+ over 10 starts for the Brewers and was not a core part of Milwaukee's postseason rotation.

This uninspiring platform performance partially explains the grade above, but only partially. We'll see how things shake out in the market when we have more signings to work from -- May is the first pitcher to land a sizable deal -- but this seems like an overpay at least in terms of years. ESPN's Kiley McDaniel projected a one-year, $14 million deal for May, while a consensus projection from various outlets looked something more like two years, $24.7 million.

The White Sox are likely banking on May's tantalizing tracking data, which in 2026 had him in the 85th percentile in fastball velocity (average of 96.8 mph) and 72nd percentile in extension. Indeed, my own projection model sees enough in May keeping his value that it suggested a three-year, $45.9 million deal would be justified, which at least is in the neighborhood of what he got from the White Sox.

As it stands, May slots in behind Grant Taylor in the revamped Chicago rotation, just ahead of Sean Burke and Luis Castillo. Ah, Castillo: Is he a cautionary tale for a White Sox approach that liked him, as it likes May, despite underwhelming results before the deal? We'll see. May is also pushing pitchers such as David Sandlin and Davis Martin down in the pecking order, though there's no guarantee he's going to be that much better than them, if at all. I've got May adding 0.9 wins to Chicago's right-now roster, which pushes its 2027 playoff odds up by about three percentage points.

That's fairly marginal when you remember that the White Sox were overachievers in 2026. It was a great story, but it also means their starting baseline is somewhere south of the 84 games they won in 2026. If they are really looking to bolster their chances heading into 2027 -- and beyond -- then opportunity cost comes into play even though the White Sox should have some remaining spending capacity, or at least you would hope so. Would a little patience have netted them someone like Sonny Gray, Michael King or Freddy Peralta?

If the White Sox still go after someone like that and the May signing doesn't end up as their one big rotation splash, then maybe we push that grade up to the C-minus range. Given what we know at the moment, though, I'm underwhelmed. -- Doolittle

Red Sox get offensive boost with Bauers addition

The deal: Four years, $58 million

Grade: A

The Red Sox weren't high on anybody's list of teams likely to sign Jake Bauers given they already have an All-Star first baseman in Willson Contreras, but this signing is an early candidate for best move of the offseason. The grade reflects two thoughts: (1) that Bauers' breakout -- he finished 11th in the majors in OPS and third in on-base percentage this past season -- is for real; and (2) that the contract is a steal at $14.5 million per year.

Bauers will be entering his age-31 season, and, of course, spent years struggling in the majors before finally figuring things out, so while there would generally be concern that his 2026 season was a fluke, all the advanced metrics suggest the opposite. His Statcast numbers: 93rd percentile bat speed, 94th percentile hard-hit rate, 93rd percentile chase rate, 98th percentile walk rate. Those are real skills that aren't going to diminish overnight and should allow him to remain a productive hitter (he even hit left-handers well, so should project as a full-time player). Everyone saw the quality of his at-bats during the postseason throughout the Milwaukee Brewers' title run; he was named MVP of the National League Championship Series.

As for the contract, compare it to Josh Naylor's deal last year, when he signed a five-year, $92.5 million contract with the Seattle Mariners. Naylor was two years younger, but he was coming off a 129-OPS+, 3.0-WAR season compared with Bauers' 140 OPS+ and 3.3 WAR. Yes, Naylor had the longer track record of success but less power and a lower OBP. Signing Bauers for $58 million looks like a potential bargain.

Contreras is under contract for 2027 with a team option for 2028 and is the better fielder, so Bauers slots in as the DH. That leaves Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu in the outfield. Masataka Yoshida is still around for one more year as a backup, and the Red Sox will likely look to trade Jarren Duran, who still has two years of team control but is estimated to make $11.1 million in arbitration. With Duran coming off a bad season at the plate, the Red Sox might non-tender him if they can't trade him.

No doubt there will be criticism that the Red Sox needed a right-handed batter instead, but they actually had a slightly higher OPS against left-handers (.734 to .710). They just needed a good hitter, regardless of which side of the plate he stands on.

Remember that they also acquired the right-handed Curtis Mead from the Washington Nationals only to see him get injured in his first game with them. He'll be back and should slot in at second base. Boston also has shortstop Franklin Arias, one of the top three or four prospects in the minors who demolished Double- and Triple-A this year. Indeed, if Bauers comes close to his 2026 numbers and Anthony hits like everyone thought he was going to in 2026, this could be one of the best lineups in the league:

LF Anthony (L)

RF Abreu (L)

1B Contreras (R)

DH Bauers (L)

CF Rafaela (R)

2B Mead (R)

C Adley Rutschman (S)

SS Arias (R) / Trevor Story (R)

3B Caleb Durbin (R)

As for the Brewers, it's sad to see a postseason hero go, although not necessarily unexpected. They could have afforded this contract, but they have first-base prospects just about ready in Andrew Fischer, who led the minors with 48 home runs, and Blake Burke, who hit 34 home runs and stole 29 bases. They also have Andrew Vaughn on hand as a placeholder if Fischer and Burke aren't ready. Plus, they might need this money to sign William Contreras to a long-term extension. The Brewers will be fine. -- Schoenfield

Braves bolster bullpen by landing Phillips
The deal: Three years, $35 million

Grade: B-

The Atlanta Braves don't go after the biggest free agents -- B.J. Upton's $75 million deal in 2013 remains the largest free agent contract in franchise history -- but president of baseball operations Alex Anthopoulos does like to strike as early as possible in the offseason, and he did that again with Evan Phillips.

Phillips will essentially take the roster spot of Raisel Iglesias, so the Braves will get a little younger and maybe a little better, although Iglesias had a good season as the closer in 2026 following some bumps in 2025. The Braves had one of the best bullpens in the majors this past year, leading in win probability added while ranking fourth in ERA and sixth in OPS allowed. Iglesias departs as a free agent, but Didier Fuentes or Robert Suarez can replace him as the ninth-inning guy, with Phillips likely slotting in as a setup man alongside lefties Dylan Lee and Dylan Dodd.

Phillips was one of the best relievers in the majors with the Dodgers in 2022-23 before suffering shoulder and elbow injuries at the end of the 2024 season and finally undergoing Tommy John surgery in June 2025. He returned to make 31 appearances with the Dodgers in 2026, finishing with 33 strikeouts and just six walks in 26 innings. The stuff looked good -- he was throwing a little harder than pre-injury -- although he did serve up five home runs, and his injury history makes a three-year deal a little risky.

The belief was that the Braves' pitching priority this offseason would be a starter, but signing Phillips will allow them to stretch out Fuentes as a starter in spring training. He does have a three-pitch arsenal in his fastball, slider and splitter, and he has thrown a curveball in the past, so as effective as Fuentes was in relief as a rookie in 2026, it makes sense to see if it can work out for him in the rotation. -- Schoenfield

Tigers kick off free agency with Pagan deal

The deal: One year, $11.5 million

Grade: C

A key reason the Detroit Tigers finished 76-86 despite a plus-71 run differential was the bullpen: Despite finishing 12th in ERA, it ranked 26th in win probability added, so it performed worse in high-leverage situations. Out with Kenley Jansen, in with Emilio Pagan, who has been the Reds' closer the past two seasons.

Jansen was only 22-for-28 in saves in 2026, so maybe Pagan is only a small upgrade, but like Jansen, Pagan has been prone to the home run, serving up 17 in 111⅓ innings over the past two seasons. The Tigers are betting that getting out of Cincinnati -- where he allowed 12 of those 17 home runs -- will help. Pagan is a three-pitch reliever, with a splitter that he throws primarily to left-handers and a cutter he throws to right-handers. But his 95 mph fastball is rather pedestrian for a modern closer, and batters have hit 12 home runs off it the past two seasons.

Pagan is also turning 36 years old and his fastball velo dropped from 95.8 mph in 2025 to 94.9 in 2026, so there are a couple of red flags here. The Tigers had to add somebody to the bullpen, and doing so before the anticipated lockout is logical, but Pagan projects as a midtier closer rather than the elite guy Detroit needs. Kyle Finnegan and Will Vest both struggled in 2026, so the Tigers could still nab a reliable right-handed setup guy. -- Schoenfield

stories.headline: Fantasy notebook: Karabell on Walker Kessler, Joel Embiid, Davion Mitchell, more
stories.summary: Eric Karabell empties out the notebook with all that he's noticing around the NBA and what it means for fantasy.
stories.body:
Los Angeles Lakers PG Luka Doncic is enjoying a remarkable start to the season, averaging 39.0 PPG and 65.8 ESPN fantasy points per game. Meanwhile, SG/PG Austin Reaves is delivering big numbers as well, with 24.7 PPG and terrific shooting. He ranks among the top 15 players on ESPN's Player Rater, and he is top 30 in points formats. Then again, these were not necessarily draft-day bargains. Investors expected monster numbers.

Lakers C Walker Kessler, however, was barely among the top 50 selections in ESPN average live drafts. It seemed optimistic at the time, since Kessler participated in a mere five games last season for the Utah Jazz before a torn labrum in his left shoulder ended his season. Kessler was off to a solid start in that small sample, averaging 14.4 PPG, 10.8 RPG and 1.8 BPG, while hitting 70.3% of his field goals. Wow, wouldn't it be nice if he could do that for 70-plus games? The Lakers hoped so when they acquired him through a July trade.

Kessler enters Tuesday's game with the Charlotte Hornets averaging 14.5 PPG, 10.9 RPG and 2.2 BPG, while hitting 68% of his field goals (which leads the NBA). Hmm, those numbers look awfully similar to last season's five-game sample, and they are tremendously valuable. Kessler is seventh on the Player Rater (roto/categories leagues) and 10th in points formats, averaging 41.4 fantasy points per game, a true fantasy MVP candidate. Tuesday's home game against Charlotte will be Kessler's first missed game, which is also significant.

Fantasy managers love all this, of course, but they also must be wondering how long these numbers can last. After all, Kessler, 25, has never delivered numbers like this for a sustained period of time. Should fantasy managers trade him? Kessler boasts more fantasy points than stars Jayson Tatum, Karl-Anthony Towns, Kevin Durant and Donovan Mitchell. A wise fantasy manager would trade Kessler for any of those fellows, of course. What about top 20 picks Amen Thompson, LaMelo Ball and Trae Young?

Much of this is dependent on your league(s) format. In points formats, where statistical versatility is not so relevant (everyone can just score and rebound and never block a shot, for example), it is smart to sell high on players off to great starts that may be overachieving and may not be so durable. In roto formats, however, players that excel in harder-to-get categories such as blocked shots, steals (Dyson Daniels, for example) and perhaps field goal shooting carry unique value.

Nobody wants to punt blocked shots in a roto league if they don't need to, but some may be forced to. Keep Kessler around in a roto format (and hope for 70-plus games), but in a points format, it may be time to perhaps seek a trade partner, just in case.

Other observations around the NBA

Miami Heat PG Davion Mitchell is another early season fantasy MVP, perhaps even more than Kessler, for he wasn't even a top 100 selection in most ESPN drafts. Mitchell is currently No. 10 on the Player Rater and barely outside the top 10 in fantasy scoring, averaging 16.7 PPG and 9.2 APG, hitting 49.7% of his field goals. Mitchell has been more durable in his career than Kessler, but mostly irrelevant for fantasy purposes. He is a former top-10 NBA draft pick by the Sacramento Kings in 2021, finally emerging in his age-28 season. The Heat, as with the Lakers, boast three players of the top 25 players in fantasy.
Speaking of the Heat, SG/SF Klay Thompson is among the most added players in ESPN standard (points) leagues. Should he be? Thompson is piling on the 3-pointers, but inconsistently. He has drained six or more 3-pointers in four games, which is great, but he also has hit two or fewer from deep five times. Thompson adds meager value with a brutal 1.4 RPG and 2.1 APG, and he has two steals in 12 games. For some reason, he's been blocking some shots, with nine in the past six games, which makes no sense. When Thompson hits 3-pointers, he matters in fantasy, but for the season, he averages only 25.4 ESPN fantasy points, well outside the top 100. You probably will not be rostering him for long in a points format.
Is it too late to rescind the praise I initially had -- after barely one week of the season -- for New Orleans Pelicans SG/PG Dejounte Murray? Murray did not play this past weekend because things have gone quite awry and he has requested a trade, one which may not be granted anytime soon. There is no telling when he will play again. Murray opened the season with 54 ESPN fantasy points and reached 39 points in four of five games, and we loved him. Then he failed to score 20 fantasy points during a controversial four-game stretch, while the team was falling apart, before sitting out. It isn't surprising that Murray is being dropped in ESPN leagues, but one should try to keep him around. When healthy, he is a solid fantasy option. Perhaps he will join another NBA team soon.
Philadelphia 76ers C Joel Embiid probably should take a break from attempting 3-pointers. Embiid, who far too often just settles for the deep outside shot because he hasn't been able to beat defenders in the paint, entered Monday having made four of 36 attempts this season, and he was 1-for-25 in his past nine games. (Then Embiid drained 2-of-4 Monday against the Brooklyn Nets, and he looked sprier than he has in years.) Even with Monday's 37-point outing, Embiid is shooting only 40% from the field. He is shooting 46.9% on 2-point attempts, which is a major problem, too. Embiid is a career 53.8% shooter on 2-pointers. That was roughly his figure last season, over 38 games. Embiid probably will not cease shooting from range, but if he isn't making shots from the elbow or converting layups, he isn't going to average 20 PPG. Be wary of investing. How many times must we learn our lesson here?
Oklahoma City Thunder C Isaiah Hartenstein averages 28.8 ESPN fantasy points per game, much like last season, but we know he can do much better. He has shown it recently, as he scored 56 ESPN fantasy points against the Clippers on Friday, which followed a 45-point effort against the Blazers two days prior. Hartenstein was fantastic in those games, scoring 20 and 21 traditional points, nabbing 16 and 11 rebounds and contributing six assists in each game. Then, on Sunday, Hartenstein scored only 3 points, giving us 16 fantasy points. Talk about inconsistency! The shorthanded Thunder may or may not need Hartenstein's scoring, but it would be nice for fantasy purposes. This fellow should be providing his solid 2024-25 numbers (11.2 PPG, 10.7 RPG, 1.1 BPG). He is not. Why? Keep investing. He isn't better than Embiid, of course, but he is more reliable.
Utah Jazz C Mo Bamba is quite the journeyman, now with his seventh franchise. He has enjoyed one fantasy relevant season, back in 2021-22 for the Orlando Magic, the team that drafted him sixth in 2018. Nobody was talking about Bamba until he dropped 26 points on Sunday night, made possible by him draining all six of his 3-point attempts. Bamba had not even attempted a 3-pointer before Sunday this season! Now he is on ESPN's most added list. His inclusion there is likely an easily reversible, short-term mistake, but the Jazz are missing so many frontcourt players (Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr., Jusuf Nurkic), someone must play. I added Bamba in a weekly league, likely to be fooled again, just to see what happens. I will likely drop him in a week.

stories.headline: JJ Gabriel confirms Man United exit as Real Madrid transfer nears
stories.summary: JJ Gabriel has confirmed his departure from Manchester United in a post on Instagram and thanked the club for the role they have played in his career.
stories.body:
JJ Gabriel has confirmed his departure from Manchester United in a post on Instagram and thanked the club for the role they have played in his career.

The 16-year-old asked to leave United in September and sources told ESPN that he is on the brink of a move to Real Madrid. He had been training in Madrid earlier this month.

"Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams," he said in the video on Instagram.

"Here, I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award, you gave me moments I'll always treasure.

"To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

"As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ."

- Man United's JJ Gabriel amid Real Madrid move talk: 'Dream to win a Ballon d'Or'

- Wayne Rooney reveals he contemplated suicide at height of Man United career

United will consider legal action if they believe illegal approaches were made while Gabriel was under contract at Old Trafford, sources said.

Gabriel's Irish passport could help facilitate the transfer under FIFA regulations governing international moves for players aged between 16 and 18, with January the first opportunity for him to be registered.

Information from ESPN's Rob Dawson contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Statue to memorialize Johnny, Matthew Gaudreau at childhood skating rink
stories.summary: The late Johnny and Matthew Gaudreau will be memorialized with a bronze statue outside of their childhood skating rink in New Jersey.
stories.body:
The late Johnny and Matthew Gaudreau will be memorialized with a bronze statue outside of their childhood skating rink in New Jersey.

Columbus Blue Jackets star Johnny Gaudreau, 31, played in the NHL for 11 seasons. Matthew Gaudreau, 29, played five seasons of professional hockey and was coaching Gloucester Catholic High School's team in New Jersey.

The Gaudreau brothers were hit and killed while riding their bicycles in New Jersey on Aug. 29, 2024. Sean M. Higgins pleaded not guilty in January 2025 and faces two counts of first-degree aggravated manslaughter, the most serious counts of his six-charge indictment, and is expected to face a jury trial in January 2027 after rejecting a plea deal.

Artist Carl LeVotch created the Gaudreau Brothers Inspiration Sculpture after watching the 2026 U.S. Olympic men's hockey team's tributes to the Gaudreau brothers during their gold-medal-winning run. He presented his sculpture concepts to their parents, Guy and Jane Gaudreau, who endorsed the project.

The 5-foot-9 bronze statue depicts the two brothers skating together. LeVotch plans to install it in front of Hollydell Ice Arena in Sewell, where the Gaudreaus first played hockey as children. It will sit on a base and collectively weigh nearly 1,000 pounds. The project has a completion date of spring 2028.

"This sculpture looks beyond remembrance as it is an invitation for every young athlete who encounters it to understand that character, compassion, and community are measures of greatness," LeVotch said in a statement.

Guy and Jane Gaudreau said that Hollydell is a special place for their family and they hope the statue inspires other young athletes.

"We hope every young player who walks through those doors sees it and is inspired to play the way John & Matty did: with heart and love for the game, and to live the way they did, with kindness on and off the ice," they said in a statement. "If it encourages even one kid to pick up a stick and follow their example, their legacy lives on."

LeVotch is working with support from Gaudreau Brothers Sculpture Project, a New Jersey-based nonprofit organization to secure funds to back the sculpture.

stories.headline: Abu Dhabi court reduces sentences for 8 in Nurmagomedov-Dvalishvili brawl
stories.summary: An Abu Dhabi court has reduced the sentences of eight defendants, including six members of Team Nurmagomedov, for their part in last week's wild hotel brawl in the UAE's capital city.
stories.body:
Abu Dhabi's Criminal Court has reduced the sentences of eight defendants convicted in connection to last week's hotel brawl involving Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili, according to the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department.

The eight defendants, including six members of Team Nurmagomedov, were originally sentenced to six months in prison. Under the revised ruling, which the ADJD released Tuesday, each defendant will instead pay a fine of 150,000 AED (approximately $40,800). The department said the reduced sentence followed a reconciliation between the parties, the mutual withdrawal of claims and appeal by the victim to the Abu Dhabi government for their release.

The altercation took place Nov. 11 in the lobby of the Yas Hilton Hotel, ahead of RAF's inaugural event in Abu Dhabi. Multiple videos captured Nurmagomedov, who is the PFL lightweight champion and younger cousin of Khabib Nurmagomedov, approach Dvalishvili from behind and slap him in the face, triggering a brawl between multiple members of both teams. Dvalishvili, who was initially arrested but released, advocated for Nurmagomedov's release Saturday.

Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili have been involved in a long-running feud, dating back to Dvalishvili's UFC title win against Umar Nurmagomedov, Usman's older brother, in January 2025. The camps were involved in a brief altercation at another RAF event in July in Dvalishvili's home country of Georgia. Over the weekend, UFC president Dana White criticized RAF's security measures, saying, "They must like it for this to happen all the time."

RAF founder Chad Bronstein told ESPN the organization regretted the incident, but pushed back on any suggestion it's becoming commonplace.

"Did they have drama in the past? Yeah," Bronstein said of Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili. "But did I think that was going to happen in Abu Dhabi? No. You can always expect there's going to be some words in a press conference ... I didn't think that would happen in a hotel lobby. How many fights have taken place at the UFC, at press conferences, in arenas? We have a great relationship with the UFC, but I think that's an unfair statement."

Bronstein added the incident did not impact RAF's recently-signed deal with the region of Abu Dhabi.

"We're already talking about new events coming up, we have a five-year deal," Bronstein said. "Saturday's event sold out Etihad Arena. I feel like there's going to be a long partnership."

On Monday, RAF announced Dvalishvili and his 21-year-old Georgian teammate Saba Lazishvili have been booked to the promotion's first event in the New York metropolitan area on Dec. 19 at Nassau Coliseum in Long Island.

Dvalishvili will face Kenzo Biyong, a former Dutch professional soccer player from the Netherlands. Lazashvili, who gained a massive online following for his participation in the hotel lobby brawl, will face the winner of a match between Sergio Garcia and Cody Garbrandt at RAF 15 on Nov. 28 in Chicago.

stories.headline: MLS wild card predictions: Who will emerge from Orlando-Cincinnati, Seattle-RSL?
stories.summary: The wild card kicks off the MLS Cup playoffs on Thursday, so who will advance to Round 1? ESPN's U.S. soccer analysts make their predictions.
stories.body:
The international break may not be quite over just yet, but in MLS, attention is already returning to the club game. That's because the opening salvos of the MLS Cup playoffs begin on Thursday with the wild-card round.

Having 18 of the league's 30 teams qualify for the postseason might make for a bloated playoff field, but who doesn't love a play-in game? Thursday night will see the eighth and ninth seeds of both conferences square off for a date with the No. 1-ranked side in the East and West.

So, Orlando City vs. FC Cincinnati, Seattle Sounders vs. Real Salt Lake, how will it all play out? Who will advance? Joseph Lowery breaks down the matchups and ESPN's U.S. soccer analysts make their predictions.

Eastern Conference
8. Orlando City vs. 9. FC Cincinnati
Star attraction: There's exactly one outfield player in MLS who's been more transformational than Antoine Griezmann -- and it's Lionel Messi. Among current players with at least 1,000 minutes this year, the FIFA World Cup winner with France is the closest to Messi when it comes to goal contributions per game. Posting a staggering 1.06 combined goals and assists per 90 minutes, Orlando City's star summer signing completely changed their fortunes.

Before Griezmann, Orlando found itself near the East's basement with 14 points in 15 games and a defense hemorrhaging goals. With the former Atlético Madrid attacker in tow, the club's points per game shot up from 0.93 to 1.68, good for the sixth-best tally in MLS since the World Cup break. The Lions are still leaking goals, though -- their 78 conceded this season is tied for the second-most in league history -- but with Griezmann's passing range and goal threat, they truly can outscore their opponents and make some noise.

X-factor: It takes a serious player to nab top billing from Evander, Cincinnati's superstar No. 10, but that's exactly what Griezmann's presence in Orlando has done. Still, both teams will take pains to limit the other's elite creator. While keeping their opponent's star quiet will be a nearly impossible feat for the second- and third-worst defensive teams in MLS, that Orlando City will be paying special attention to Evander will open space for Pavel Bucha.

Outside of Evander and the team's center-back corps, no Cincinnati regular touches the ball more than Bucha. According to American Soccer Analysis, the Czechia international central midfielder takes 8.1% of his team's touches. Bucha's service even prompted manager Pat Noonan to play him as a right wingback earlier this year. Back in the center, the 28-year-old will have a chance to provide the creative touch for the visitors.

Tactical wrinkle: It's all well and good for Cincinnati to have Griezmann at the top of the scouting report and for Orlando to do the same with Evander. Slowing those players down is another matter entirely. How effectively each team accomplishes that task could decide Thursday's match.

Orlando had exactly one true center back in its squad on Decision Day. The Lions have been hurting for quality central defenders, and that pain only increased when Robin Jansson went down with a season-ending injury. Just how will interim manager Martín Perelman compensate for being perilously thin in the back?

Cincinnati, for its part, spent more on salaries for defenders than any other team this year as of the MLS Players Association's May release. Try as Noonan might, defensive stability has evaded his team. They'll need to find another level without the ball to keep Orlando's high-powered attack quiet.

Predictions
Orlando has the luxury of playing at home and will have the best player on the field in Griezmann. Between the Frenchman, Martín Ojeda, Marco Pasalic, and U.S. men's national teamer Justin Ellis, Orlando City's attacking arsenal will be too much for Cincinnati to handle. -- Lowery

Neither of these teams is very good defensively, but Cincinnati seemed to get its act together toward the end of the season. Evander vs. Griezmann should be fun, but I expect Cincinnati to come out on top. -- Jeff Carlisle

You can't overlook the form of Griezmann. He's got nine goal contributions in his past seven games for Orlando and will likely be the difference-maker in this matchup. -- Cesar Hernandez

This match feels more like a Round 1 matchup with MVP finalist Evander taking on Newcomer of the Year finalist Griezmann. Despite two good sides, Orlando should be able to capitalize on the Frenchman's magic to advance. -- Lizzy Becherano

Western Conference
8. Seattle Sounders vs. 9. Real Salt Lake
Star attraction: There was no bigger breakout star in MLS this year than Real Salt Lake striker Sergi Solans. The Spaniard has taken an atypical path, beginning in the Girona academy before heading to Oregon State, being drafted by Salt Lake, going back to school, transferring to UCLA, and now shining in MLS. Solans finished tied for eighth in non-penalty goals (15) during his rookie campaign. So impressive was the 23-year-old that RSL handed him a new contract months into the campaign.

Even with Zavier Gozo's August departure and Diego Luna 's season-ending injury, Solans managed six goals in his final eight games of the regular season. The No. 9 is a workhorse atop head coach Pablo Mastroeni's 3-4-3 attacking setup and it's hard to picture him lasting long in MLS before a European club comes knocking.

X-factor: The Sounders were getting desperate. They'd lost eight games in a row from the middle of May to the middle of August, a streak that seemed unthinkable for a team with Seattle's level of depth and experience. But with a growing injury list and a lengthy barren run, the team needed change. Enter: star striker Dejan Joveljic. In their first notable acquisition involving a transfer fee since Pedro de la Vega joined in 2024, the Sounders spent $6 million in a cash-for-player trade to snag Joveljic from Sporting Kansas City.

Immediately thrust into manager Brian Schmetzer's starting lineup, the Serbia international bagged a brace in his Seattle debut and collected four goals in his first five games. Since then? He's scored just one in six matches. Reliant on service, Joveljic doesn't have the benefit of being surrounded by a consistent or balanced attack. There's a reason his goals have come in bunches, after all.

If the Sounders manage to feed Joveljic on Thursday, they'll put themselves in the driver's seat. If not, the striker's barren run will likely continue as his team's playoff run ends.

Tactical wrinkle: In an underrated pickup, Real Salt Lake signed Canada's starting center back at the World Cup Luc de Fougerolles on loan from Fulham in the summer. The 21-year-old has been tasked with a fascinating role by Mastroeni -- one not dissimilar to how Wilfried Nancy used Steven Moreira during the Columbus Crew 's MLS Cup run in 2023. Constantly encouraged to push into the attack from his right-sided center-back spot, De Fougerolles leads all central defenders with at least 500 minutes this year in passes and touch share in the final third, as per ASA. The next closest true center back to De Fougerolles? Moreira himself.

With the Canadian eager to help RSL overload the attack, Seattle will have its hands full maintaining numerical parity in the back. But if the Sounders can stymie Salt Lake's aggressive possession positioning, they'll have chances to attack the visitors on the break.

Predictions
In the three years of MLS' current playoff format, the lower-seeded wild-card team has won just once in six tries. The odds, then, are in Seattle's favor despite Salt Lake's stronger form heading into this meeting. -- Lowery

The rosters of both teams have been in flux this season, Seattle due to injuries and RSL due to the same plus the transfer of Gozo. But of the two teams, Seattle has the experience to progress, especially in midfield with Hassani Dotson and Cristian Roldan. -- Carlisle

It's going to be a tough one for Brian Schmetzer & Co., but they have enough playoff experience to get this over the line. Keep an eye on Albert Rusnák, who has a goal and two assists in his past two appearances. -- Hernandez

The Sounders went through a difficult season, but Schmetzer's experience in the league can work to out-coach Salt Lake to earn the victory. -- Becherano

stories.headline: Fernando Alonso confirmed for Dakar Rally with Aston Martin
stories.summary: Fernando Alonso will return to the Dakar Rally in January next year as Aston Martin prepares for a surprise debut at the legendary rally raid event.
stories.body:
Fernando Alonso will return to the Dakar Rally in January next year as Aston Martin prepares for a surprise debut at the legendary rally raid event.

The Aston Martin Formula 1 driver, who last took part in the Dakar in 2020 with Toyota, will be joined in a three-car line-up by nine-time world rally champion Sebastien Loeb and world rally raid champion Lucas Moraes.

Working alongside rallying experts Prodrive, Aston Martin has produced a competition-ready rally car that has a tie-in with a military vehicle it developed for use in the video game Call of Duty, Modern Warfare 4. Known as the Dreadnought in both the virtual and real world, the rally car shares very little other than its name with its video-gaming cousin and has been designed specifically to take part in the Dakar Rally, which will return to the continent of Africa next year for the first time since 2007.

Alonso will be joined in his Dreadnought by Marc Coma -- the same co-driver he had in 2020 and a five-time Dakar motorcycle category winner.

"After deciding to continue racing in Formula One with the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team, I thought carefully about Dakar," Alonso, who signed a deal to race with Aston Martin in F1 in September, said.

"In the end, the decision became simple. I wanted to embrace the challenge completely and take on both Formula One and the Dakar Rally in the same year. In 2020, Dakar was one of the most challenging and enjoyable experiences of my career.

"I have enormous respect for this race and the specialists who have mastered it. Having Marc alongside me again is very important, and with Aston Martin, Prodrive, Sébastien and Lucas we have an exceptional team.

"Formula One remains my priority. But I am a racing driver, and challenges like this are why I love competing. I'm looking forward to seeing what we can achieve."

The legendary Dakar Rally was born from a series of rallies that ran from Europe to Africa in the 1970s and held its inaugural event from Paris to Dakar in 1979. Although the route changed through the two continents in the 1990s and early 2000s, the event retained its name before it eventually left Africa in 2008 due to security threats in Mauritania.

Initially the rally found a new home in South America from 2009 to 2019 before moving to Saudi Arabia in 2020, which was the event Alonso took part in and finished 13th driving for Toyota.

In October, it was announced the 2027 event would run from Portugal to Morocco due to security concerns linked to the U.S.-Israel war on Iran and deadly attacks by Yemen's Houthis on Saudi Arabia.

The event will now start in the Algarve and finish in Marrakech, stretching across 12 stages and totaling 4,341km in length. The 2027 Dakar Rally will get underway on January 9 and conclude on January 23.

stories.headline: Nike replaces Adidas as UEFA ball provider to restyle Champions League
stories.summary: The Champions League ball will have a new look next season after Nike replaced Adidas as UEFA's official provider.
stories.body:
The Champions League ball will have a new look next season after Nike replaced Adidas as UEFA's official provider.

A match ball manufactured by Adidas, with the famous star-studded ball used for Europe's premier competition, will be used for the final time in the 2026-27 final.

There has been no confirmation as to whether the new Nike ball will retain the star pattern used in the competitions logo. UEFA said in a statement: "Further details on the match ball designs will be revealed in due course.."

- Why the Champions League's iconic 'star' match ball could soon be replaced

From 2027-28, U.S. brand Nike will take over as the official ball supplier for UEFA for the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League.

German brand Adidas had been the ball supplier for the UEFA Champions League since 2001 but their long-standing association with the competition is now coming to an end.

Nike went into exclusive talks in April with the agency that handles all commercial deals for UEFA club competitions, a subsidiary of United States-based Relevent.

Relevent was appointed last year by the commercial joint venture between UEFA and the increasingly influential European Football Clubs group, which has seen long-standing sponsor deals end.

Relevent was co-founded by Miami Dolphins owner Stephen Ross and also has a long-term deal with UEFA to market commercial rights for national team competitions.

Total broadcast and sponsor revenue for UEFA men's club competitions is projected to rise above 5 billion euros ($5.5 billion) starting next season.

Camilo Andrade, Vice President and General Manager of Nike Football, said: "We are excited and honoured to return to the UEFA Champions League, one of football's biggest stages, after more than two decades, and to bring Nike match balls across UEFA's men's club competitions, including all three major competitions for the first time.

"Football is the world's game, and the ball is at the centre of it, the one thing every player, in every competition, has in common. This is a long-term commitment for Nike. We will listen to the athlete's voice, push the edges of innovation, honour the prestige and tradition of these competitions, and make sure the ball represents the instinct, creativity and joy football brings to billions of fans."

Guy-Laurent Epstein, Co-Managing Director UC3 -- which unites UEFA to Europe's clubs -- said: "We are delighted to welcome Nike as the official match ball provider for UEFA men's club competitions from 2027. Nike brings an incredible combination of sporting heritage, creativity and cultural influence, with an ability to connect with fans around the world. We look forward to working together, both on and off the pitch, to deliver innovation, quality and performance at every level of European club football."

Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Toronto Tempo win 2027 WNBA draft lottery, land No. 1 pick
stories.summary: The Tempo won the WNBA draft lottery Sunday night, earning the No. 1 pick and potentially the chance to draft USC star JuJu Watkins. The Comets will choose second, followed by the Mystics.
stories.body:
The Toronto Tempo will have the No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA draft after winning the draft lottery Sunday night.

After completing its inaugural season in 2026, Toronto becomes the first franchise to have the top pick heading into its second season since the Dream in 2009, when Atlanta selected Angel McCoughtry. The Tempo will make their selection April 12.

Lottery odds are based on teams' two-year cumulative records, except for Portland and Toronto, which were expansion teams in 2026. Their odds were solely based on their records from this past season.

The Houston Comets, formerly the Connecticut Sun (22-66), and Toronto (11-33) had the best odds to land the No. 1 pick, each with 329 chances out of 1,000. This marked the first time since 2015 that two teams had the same odds for the first selection.

The Sun, relocating to Texas from Connecticut this offseason, went 1-2 against Toronto in 2026 -- which is the first tiebreaker -- so the franchise couldn't fall past the third pick. Toronto was guaranteed at least the fourth selection.

"I [felt] like something amazing was going to happen," said Tempo forward Aneesah Morrow, the team's lottery representative. "We're here now ... The future is bright. We have great and amazing players, and we have a country on our back. It feels different when you play like that."

Houston will select second in the draft. All of the other selections are in line with what the odds projected heading into Sunday. Washington, which had the next-best odds after acquiring Chicago's first-round pick in the trade that sent Ariel Atkins to the Sky, will pick third.

Seattle will select at No. 4, followed by Portland at No. 5. The Los Angeles Sparks have the sixth and seventh picks -- one that is their own and the other acquired from Phoenix in the Kelsey Plum trade in August.

USC's JuJu Watkins is projected to go No. 1 in ESPN's latest mock draft released Thursday, with Texas' Madison Booker slotted at No. 2.

Notre Dame's Hannah Hidalgo, Virginia's Kymora Johnson, LSU's Mikaylah Williams, Kansas' S'Mya Nichols and Sarah Cisse of France are projected to round out the lottery picks.

The Tempo had a strong start to their season before veteran Brittney Sykes was sidelined indefinitely because of a plantar fascia injury. After she went down, Toronto went 4-21, including a 12-game losing streak. But Sykes and Marina Mabrey combined to form one of the highest-scoring backcourts in the league.

Toronto has some young talent in Morrow, whom the team acquired in a midseason trade, and last year's No. 6 pick Kiki Rice, who was the team's third-leading scorer but missed nearly two months because of a Grade 2 left ankle sprain. The combination of Mabrey, Sykes and Rice gives the Tempo perimeter depth. However, they are somewhat thin in the front court.

"[Toronto] is amazing," Morrow said. "Ever since I walked in the locker room, from the beginning, I was able to see the chemistry ... it's all about building the future of the Toronto franchise."

The WNBA schedule will increase from 44 to 50 games in the 2027 season, making it the longest in league history. The added games were part of the new collective bargaining agreement, which also vastly increased pay, secured a $2.2 billion media deal and slated six expansion teams to join the league between 2024 and 2030.

The 2027 WNBA season is expected to start May 7 and has a latest possible end date of Oct. 24, sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou last week.

"We're excited about the momentum; it's never been stronger," said Bethany Donaphin, senior vice president and head of WNBA league operations. "We think there's a demand, and we're excited to expand to 50 games."

The rest of the first-round draft order is: No. 8 New York, No. 9 Dallas, No. 10 Indiana, No. 11 Chicago, No. 12 Chicago, No. 13 Dallas, No. 14 Golden State and No. 15 Minnesota.

stories.headline: Kangaroos bounce Kiwis for fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup title
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have won a fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup, toppling New Zealand 32-12 in Brisbane.
stories.body:
The Kangaroos have punished a disappointing New Zealand, with Reece Walsh running riot in a 32-12 World Cup final waltz.

There was an expectation the Kiwis, searching for their second Cup title and first since 2008, would push Australia all the way after a two-point loss in a pulsating tournament opener.

But the visitors struggled from the outset in Brisbane on Sunday night, Jamayne Isaako's kick-off floating long in a sign of things to come.

Walsh dazzled at fullback for the Kangaroos, his pace, vision and wicked footwork too much as he helped lay on two tries and generally wreak havoc around the ruck and close to the line.

Conversely, Walsh's New Zealand opposite Kalyn Ponga -- International Rugby League's Golden Boot winner on Thursday night -- was unable to get into game.

Australian hooker Harry Grant and halves Tom Dearden and Cam Munster completely outplayed their error-riddled opposites, while the Kangaroos' pack muscled up.

Dearden laid on two first-half tries for Liam Martin with well-timed short balls, while Bradman Best was rewarded for an inspired chase-down tackle of Jahrome Hughes with a try soon after.

When Tom Trbojevic scored to begin the second half it was 28-6 and effectively game over.

Jack Bostock completed his breakout season with a try in each half for Australia.

It was the Kangaroos' fourth consecutive title and 10th in the last 11 tournaments, dating back to 1975.

stories.headline: Fantasy football consistency ratings: 2024 to 2026
stories.summary: The consistency ratings weigh both how consistent and how start-worthy players have been from 2024 to 2026.
stories.body:
Updated Nov. 17, 2026 (through Week 10 of 2026)

How consistency ratings work
Using fantasy points determined by ESPN's standard scoring, the charts contained in this column rate players based upon how consistently reliable they have been during the 2024 through 2026 seasons, a span of 46 weeks' worth of games (18 weeks apiece in 2024 and 2025, 10 so far in 2026). For IDPs (individual defensive players), the scoring from our weekly rankings is used: solo tackle (1.5), assisted tackle (0.75), tackle for loss (2), sack (4), interception (5), forced fumble (4), fumble recovery (4), touchdown (6), safety (2), pass defended (1.5). To familiarize you with the terminology and column headers listed in the charts below:

Start%: The player's "start percentage," which shows how often he earned a start in an ESPN standard PPR (points per reception) league. This is his number of "starts" -- those defined below -- divided by his number of scheduled team games.

CR: The player's "consistency rating," which is calculated as his weekly standard deviation divided by his PPR fantasy points per game average. This is meant to identify the players who were most consistently close to their weekly averages. The lower the number, the more consistent the player. Again, lower numbers are better.

nPPR%: The player's start percentage using non-PPR scoring, using ESPN's standard scoring settings without any points per reception.

FPTS/G: The player's average PPR fantasy points scored per game.

Start: The number of times that the player's point total in a given week was worthy of having had him active in an ESPN standard PPR league.

Star: The number of times the player's point total ranked among the best at his position.

Stiff: The number of times the player's point total ranked among the worst at his position, making almost any waiver-wire option a smarter choice.

These are the benchmarks for what constitutes a "start," "star" or "stiff" performance:

Sat: The number of times the player sat out a game. Players are not charged "stiff" points for sitting out, nor does it impact their overall consistency rating (CR), but it hurts their overall start percentage.

Players must have a start rate of at least 20% in either standard PPR or non-PPR scoring, rank among the top 20 quarterbacks, tight ends or kickers, top 50 running backs or wide receivers, or top 40 defensive linemen, linebackers or defensive backs, in terms of total fantasy points at their position from 2024 to 2026, or are averaging at least 50 snaps per game, for inclusion in the chart. All defense/special teams are included regardless of whether they meet those minimums.

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball reactions to MLB offseason trades, signings
stories.summary: Track all the latest MLB free agency and trade news with fantasy baseball analysis from Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell.

stories.body:
Tracking the offseason MLB trades and signings with fantasy baseball implications for the upcoming season, Eric Karabell and Tristan H. Cockcroft will analyze and provide an outlook for all of the key players involved.

With the World Series behind us, players were allowed to sign with new teams beginning Nov. 2, although typically things don't really start to heat up until the league's annual winter meetings. This year's meetings are scheduled to take place in San Diego from Dec. 7 to Dec. 9.

However, as the current collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, the 2027 season (as well as the financial rules that will govern it), players and teams alike might end up waiting until after the dust settles on negotiations and a potential lockout before inking any new deals.

In any event, as any contracts are signed or trades get agreed to, this is the place to find all of the fantasy fallout of those deals. Be sure to check back throughout the hot stove season for updates.

Below, you will find a list of some of the top free agents at each position. Players labeled with a (Q) have received a qualifying offer from their current team and have until Nov. 17 to accept it or decline and become a free agent. Players coming from Japan/Korea who were posted by their current team have a Dec. 1 deadline to reach a deal with an MLB club to play in the United States in 2027.

Note: Not every transaction warrants the attention of fantasy managers, but for those signings and trades that do merit analysis, you'll find them listed below. Players will be separated by position and then listed in chronological order of the move within each positional grouping, with the latest news coming first. Also included are links to any standalone analysis stories and/or videos regarding major free agent signings and trades. Players who end up re-signing with their previous team will not always be included.

Catcher
Some free agents: Carson Kelly, Ryan Jeffers (Q), Tyler Stephenson, Kyle Higashioka, Gary Sanchez, James McCann, Travis d'Arnaud, Austin Hedges

First base

Jake Bauers signs with Red Sox
Bauers, 31, comes off the best season of his journeyman career, posting an .873 OPS with 26 homers and 86 RBIs for the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. He admits that he considered retirement as recently as two years ago, but he stuck around for the health benefits. Good timing. Bauers gets a four-year deal with the Red Sox, where he and right-handed-hitting Willson Contreras should make for a formidable 1-2 punch in the middle of the lineup, while sharing 1B/DH duties.

While Bauers was a top-40 hitter in points formats and roto/categories leagues last season, fantasy managers probably shouldn't expect the same kind of production moving forward, even as he performs half the time at hitter-friendly Fenway Park. Bauers had never hit more than 12 home runs in any prior season and, even now, he remains a career .223 hitter with a 2.0 career WAR.

Maybe the solid 16.3% walk rate and .218 ISO will continue, but preliminary results in NFBC drafts have Bauers going just inside the top 150. Perhaps he gets a bump for heading to Boston, but likely only a modest one. -- Karabell (11/13)

Starting pitcher
Dustin May signs with White Sox
May, 29, made 31 mostly league-average starts for the Cardinals and eventual champion Brewers this season -- many of them quite abbreviated. In fact, he ended up averaging fewer than four innings over his 10 Brewers starts and he did not qualify for the ERA title. The desperate White Sox figure to allow May to go deeper into games, but that comes at a cost, since he posted a 4.70 ERA and a 1.32 WHIP with only 0.4 bWAR last season.

Hey, at least May stayed healthy, which is a feat for him. Plus, he was a bit unlucky, as his 3.54 FIP indicates. However, that doesn't mean May warrants inclusion in ESPN standard drafts, with a preliminary points-league rank outside the top 75 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/17)

Relief pitcher
RHP Emilio Pagan signs with Tigers
Pagan, 35, saved 57 games for the Cincinnati Reds over the past two seasons, although his 2025 numbers were rather ordinary (3.38 ERA, 25.9% K rate). Still, this is a franchise that desired Kenley Jansen and let him save 22 games last season even though there were better pitchers in the bullpen. Pagan produced nearly identical stats to Jansen. In other words, Pagan isn't so valuable -- but if all you care about are saves in a roto format, a healthy Pagan should provide at least 25 of them. -- Karabell (11/13)

RHP Evan Phillips signs with Braves
Phillips, 32, posted a 2.36 ERA over parts of six seasons for the Los Angeles Dodgers. He also accrued 42 combined saves during 2023 and 2024. He missed most of 2025 dealing with Tommy John surgery and returned last season to pitch 26 effective innings. Additionally, Phillips has never permitted a run over 18⅓ postseason innings. NBA Trade Lab: Dejounte Murray's trade request

After formally requesting a trade last Friday, New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray has unsurprisingly been the player most involved in fan-created trades over the past seven days in our NBA Trade Lab.

The Spurs traded Murray to the Hawks in 2022 for a massive haul: three first-round picks (including the Hawks' pick in the upcoming 2027 draft) and one first-round pick swap. At the time, Murray was viewed as a burgeoning young star with a strong impact on both sides of the ball. In Atlanta he expanded his offensive game, but his defensive impact, as measured by Net Points, fell off a cliff. In 2024, the Hawks sent him to the Pelicans in exchange for a package that included two first-round picks and Dyson Daniels, who went on to win Most Improved Player the following season.

Now in 2026, it appears likely Murray will be on the move again, but his market is difficult to read. His impact metrics have been on the decline, and he's making over $30 million for the next two seasons after turning 30 years old. At the same time, he is undoubtedly a talented player who could certainly find a renaissance in the right situation. Let's look at some of the top fan-created trades to see what fans are thinking might be a realistic deal.

Trade No. 1
Pelicans get: Jalen Green

Phoenix Suns get: Dejounte Murray

Green and Murray are similar in many ways, so a straight-up swap could make sense for both teams. Green is a talented scorer, but he lacks consistency and doesn't offer the ancillary skills to buoy him at a constant floor of positive impact. He is also only 24, the same age as Warriors Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, so the Pelicans could see room to further develop him in their system.

For the Suns, this would be a bet on their system. They have built a menacing defensive identity over the past two seasons and often punch above their weight through effort and hustle. Bringing Murray into this system could help to revive some of the defensive aspects of his game that have faded in recent years.

Trade No. 2
Pelicans get: Four second-round picks

Charlotte Hornets get: Murray

In this unusual deal, the Pelicans get no players back. It is a valid trade because of the $40 million trade exception that the Hornets received in the LaMelo Ball trade. Four second-round picks may not sound like much, but in the process the Pelicans would also open up a $32 million trade exception of their own and would completely clear Murray's money off their books without receiving any undesirable contracts in return.

The Hornets' offense has been really struggling this season, ranking last in Offensive Net Points per game, after losing their offensive engine in LaMelo Ball. Trading for Murray could inject some life into their offense, strengthening their guard play while they wait for Kon Knueppel to return from injury and Coby White to return to form after a slow start to his season.

Trade No. 3
Pelicans get: De'Aaron Fox and Spurs 2029 first-round pick

San Antonio Spurs get: Murray and Herb Jones

The Pelicans here get a proven winner and veteran presence in Fox, who could help to mentor Jeremiah Fears and their other young players throughout their roster. They also receive a 2029 first-round pick to build their future draft capital.

The Spurs are rolling right now and Fox has been playing great, so this would likely be a trade they consider only if things start to go downhill a bit and they decide they want to get off Fox's contract. San Antonio might be more interested in Murray than other teams, since he played some of his best basketball there. In this deal they also receive a very valuable player in Jones, whose defensive ability could slot perfectly into the Spurs' lineups and make the Victor Wembanyama-anchored defense even more impenetrable. -- Benjamin Tiemeyer

Have any more ideas on what move the Pelicans should make involving Dejounte Murray? Build it in the NBA Trade Lab, then submit your trade to let fans vote on it from both sides.

Victor Wembanyama officially launched his 2027 NBA MVP campaign on Wednesday with a statistical performance not seen since Wilt Chamberlain.

The Spurs star posted 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks in a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks, becoming the first player to achieve a 52/24/8 line since blocks became an official statistic in 1973-74.

Chamberlain, the Hall of Fame center, is the only player in league history to match or exceed those numbers thanks to a 55-point, 29-rebound, 17-block performance for the Philadelphia Warriors against the New York Knicks in 1961.

This was truly rare air: Wembanyama posted the NBA's first 52/24 line since Chamberlain in 1969 and the first 50-20 game since Luka Doncic in 2022.

"It should be more like this," Wembanyama promised. "More often."

With Doncic and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander emerging as early MVP favorites, Wembanyama threw his hat into the ring on a wild night that easily could have gotten even wilder. The 2023 No. 1 pick set a new career high for scoring by shooting 16-of-28 from the field and 19-of-23 from the free throw line against an overmatched Dallas front line, but he made only one of his eight 3-point attempts.

"I can still do more," Wembanyama said, noting that he's shooting a career-low 24 percent on 3-pointers this season. "My shots weren't falling tonight and that forces me into a style of play that is exhausting. I can do it. The proof is there."

After stumbling out of the gate with an 0-2 start, the Spurs have won six straight games and Wembanyama has started to find his scoring groove. The Thunder held the French center to 12 points on 1-of-13 shooting on opening night, but he has scored at least 36 points in three of his past four games and is on track to lead the NBA in blocks for the fourth straight season.

Go ahead and brace for more fireworks: Wembanyama and the Spurs are set to face the NBA's three worst defenses -- the Kings, Suns and Bulls -- over the next week.

Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected
The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions.

Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge.

For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. However, despite a mandate to remain under the second apron, New York is allowed to keep Wiseman and Bruce Brown to start the season.

The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET.

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023.

Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace. Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility.

The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Sept. 26

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash
The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.summary: Manchester City are in talks with Matheus Nunes about extending his contract at the Etihad Stadium, sources have told ESPN.
stories.body:
Manchester City are in talks with Matheus Nunes about extending his contract at the Etihad Stadium, sources have told ESPN.

Nunes has a deal until 2028, but City are keen to agree fresh terms. Negotiations are ongoing, although sources have told ESPN that talks are not yet at an advanced stage.

The Portugal international is closing in on 150 appearances for the club after arriving from Wolves in 2023. Initially joining as a midfielder, he was converted to a full-back under former boss Pep Guardiola.

Nunes appeared in 34 of City's 38 Premier League games last season with his form convincing club bosses to strengthen other areas of the squad over the summer instead of at right-back.

Meanwhile, City are facing a decision about whether to keep midfielder Mateo Kovacic. The Croatian is out of contract at the end of the season and can negotiate with clubs outside the Premier League from January.

Kovacic has struggled for game time so far this season and has made just one Premier League start under new manager Enzo Maresca.
